root_cause.text: In `io_uring/zcrx`, `io_zcrx_map_area()` could initialize `area->mem.page_sg_table` and then return on `io_populate_area_dma()` failure without freeing it, because the error path was incorrectly gated by `area->is_mapped`, so the cleanup for non-`dmabuf` mappings was skipped and the `sgtable` leaked.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says `io_zcrx_map_area()` “will have an initialised and not freed table” when `io_populate_area_dma()` fails, and “!is_mapped prevents that”; the patch fixes this by adding `dma_unmap_sgtable(ifq->dev, &area->mem.page_sg_table, DMA_FROM_DEVICE, IO_DMA_ATTR);` when `ret && !area->mem.is_dmabuf`, showing the missing failure-path cleanup in `io_uring/zcrx.c`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix DMA mapping cleanup on io_zcrx_map_area() failure for non-dmabuf memory.
intent_record.what: In io_zcrx_map_area(), after calling io_populate_area_dma(ifq, area), the code now checks `if (ret && !area->mem.is_dmabuf)` and, on failure for non-dmabuf memory, calls `dma_unmap_sgtable(ifq->dev, &area->mem.page_sg_table, DMA_FROM_DEVICE, IO_DMA_ATTR)` before the existing `if (ret == 0) area->is_mapped = true;` path.
intent_record.how: If DMA population fails for a regular page-based area, the newly added unmap call releases the previously created DMA scatter-gather mapping, preventing a DMA mapping leak or stale mapping state. Successful mappings still behave the same and mark the area as mapped.

grouping_result.intent: Fix DMA mapping cleanup on io_zcrx_map_area() failure for non-dmabuf memory.

relevance_review.reason: The group’s intent matches the root cause exactly: it fixes cleanup in io_zcrx_map_area() when DMA population fails for non-dmabuf memory, which addresses the leaked page_sg_table caused by the incorrect error-path gating.

candidates.rationale: This call can fail after initializing the DMA/sg table setup for a non-dmabuf area, and the subsequent failure path in the pre-fix code did not properly free the partially initialized `area->mem.page_sg_table`, leading to a leak.

This condition only marks the area as mapped on success; in the buggy version, cleanup on failure was incorrectly gated by `area->is_mapped`, so when `ret != 0` the cleanup for the allocated sgtable was skipped.

vuln_statements.explanation: This success-only branch is the point where the pre-fix logic set up the mapped state and, by implication, controlled whether later cleanup would run. The vulnerability root cause states the failure path was incorrectly gated by is_mapped, causing the sgtable allocated during io_populate_area_dma() to be skipped on error.

This call can partially initialize DMA/sg-table state before failing. In the buggy code, a failure here left area->mem.page_sg_table allocated without cleanup, which is the leak described in the root cause.

In this commit, `io_zcrx_map_area_umem()` now does `if (i != area->nia.num_niovs) { __io_zcrx_unmap_area(ifq, area, i); return -EINVAL; }`, so partial mappings are explicitly unwound on failure instead of relying on later cleanup. `io_zcrx_map_area()` also only sets `area->is_mapped = true` when `ret == 0`, and returns the error code directly.
